title: Validating a Precision Livestock Farming Method to Determine Individual, Daily Grazing Feed Intake
content: Accurate measurement of individual dry matter intake (DMI) is fundamental to eval-uating feed efficiency and other performance traits in beef cattle but remains difficult un-der grazing conditions. The study objective was to externally validate a previously devel-oped long short-term memory (LSTM) model for predicting individual grazing DMI using independent cattle populations and grazing environments that differed from those used during model development. A total of 113 grazing beef heifers representing four cohorts were evaluated across three grazing performance tests conducted in West Virginia and Georgia during 2024. Individual DMI was predicted using the LSTM model from passively collected animal and environmental data (ML-DMI). Ground-truth DMI was inde-pendently estimated using titanium dioxide as an external marker and forage digestibility (TiO₂-DMI). Agreement between methods was evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE), matched-pairs analysis, Bland–Altman analysis, and a repeated-measures linear mixed model. Daily RMSE was 1.60 kg·d⁻¹ and decreased to 1.35 kg·d⁻¹ when DMI was av-eraged across validation days. Mean difference between methods was −0.097 kg·d⁻¹ (P = 0.45), and DMI-estimation method was not significant in the mixed model (P = 0.65). These results support the application of the LSTM model to independent cattle populations and dissimilar grazing environments.
